problem_statement: The HaiderAziz428/Wardrobe.com project is a static fashion-commerce template with a homepage (brand/nav/cart icon, hero CTA, Featured products and Latest products grids), an all-products page (index2.html), and a contacts page (contacts.html). The Featured products grid carries a 'Shop by category' filter (the '.shopfilter' tab row: All / Tops / Footwear / Bottoms) with a live count readout, and shoppers should be able to reach their bag from every page. Complete and repair the shopping experience so it is consistent, responsive, visually on-brand, and actually wired: (a) add a shared 'Your bag' cart bar to EVERY commerce page (home, all-products, contacts) so the bag summary is reachable site-wide, styled to match the Wardrobe look; (b) keep the shop-by-category tab row from overflowing the 390px mobile viewport on the homepage and all-products page (let the tabs wrap / use a fluid row instead of a fixed-width non-wrapping row; do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden); (c) keep the category filter and its Featured product grid visually faithful to the reference Wardrobe layout — the filtered cards must sit in a clean readable grid with a legible active tab, not a collapsed/overlapping/clipped row with an illegible active chip; and (d) wire the category tabs so that clicking one filters the Featured grid AND updates the count readout (the '#shopfilter-readout' 'Showing N of M · Category' line), not merely highlight the tab. Preserve the Wardrobe identity, navigation, footer, local product imagery, and the desktop/tablet layout.
required_content: Add a shared 'Your bag' cart bar (class 'cart-bar', containing the text 'Your bag') to the header area of ALL THREE commerce pages (index.html, index2.html, contacts.html) so the bag summary appears consistently site-wide, not only on the product pages.

Keep the '.shopfilter' shop-by-category tab row responsive so the mobile homepage and mobile all-products page have NO horizontal overflow at 390px (wrap the tabs / fluid row). Do not clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width.
Keep the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts free of horizontal overflow.

Keep the category filter and its Featured product grid visually faithful to the reference layout: the product cards must sit in a clean, non-overlapping, non-clipped grid and the active category tab must stay legible (do not collapse the cards into an overlapping/shingled row or make the active tab dark-text-on-dark).

Wire the category tabs (class 'shopfilter__tab') so that clicking one filters the Featured grid to the matching products AND updates the count readout '#shopfilter-readout' to 'Showing N of M · Category' (e.g. clicking Footwear yields 'Showing 1 of 4 · Footwear') — the post-click terminal state must reflect the real result, not stay at 'Showing 4 of 4 · All'.
Do not damage the existing Wardrobe branding, navigation buttons (Home / Products / Contacts), hero, product grids, footer, contact details, or local product imagery on any page.
design_constraints: Preserve the Wardrobe identity: italic serif logo with the red 'robe.' accent, white/gray commerce surface, simple nav buttons, cart icon, existing product grids and footer.
Do not replace the pages, the product grids, or the category filter with a new app shell, modal-only interface, external design system, or unrelated layout.
Do not remove the shop-by-category filter, the shared cart bar, the count readout, the nav buttons, product cards, or footer links.
Do not add npm dependencies, remote scripts, remote fonts, remote images, generated build outputs, or unrelated file churn.

The category tab row and the cart bar must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, and must render in the Wardrobe white/red palette with a clean, legible product grid.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the responsive homepage nav, hero, and initial product content; mobile_initial is where the toolbar overflow is observed and repaired.
desktop_featured_products and desktop_latest_products protect the homepage readiness toolbars after scroll, where the cues must remain visible.
desktop_all_products and desktop_all_products_deep protect the all-products route and deeper product grid after scroll.
mobile_all_products protects narrow-viewport layout of the all-products readiness toolbar, the second place the overflow is repaired.
desktop_contact protects the existing contact route and nav after changing the shared static CSS.
The horizontal-overflow discriminator is measured on the mobile grid states; desktop and tablet stay within the viewport in every leg.

change_completion: The shared 'Your bag' cart bar appears in the header of all three commerce pages (home, all-products, contacts).
The mobile homepage and mobile all-products page have no horizontal overflow after the tab-row repair.
Clicking a category tab filters the Featured grid and updates the count readout to 'Showing N of M · Category'.
content_asset_continuity: The product grids stay grounded in the repo's local product imagery; no external or placeholder media.
Existing brand, nav, footer, contact details, and product content are preserved.
design_consistency: The category filter and Featured grid keep the Wardrobe white/ivory + red #ff523b palette, a clean non-overlapping grid, and a legible active tab, visually faithful to the reference.
The same cart bar component is consistent across all three pages; the hero, product grids, and footer remain visually recognizable.
interaction_continuity: The category tab updates the '#shopfilter-readout' 'Showing N of M · Category' count on click (the post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the stale 'Showing 4 of 4 · All').
regression: Home, all-products, and contacts pages retain their original Wardrobe branding, nav labels, and imagery.
No new dependency, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced.
responsive: The homepage and all-products page have no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile states.
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow.

author_notes: Slot slot_168 targets the HaiderAziz428/Wardrobe.com static fashion-commerce template, an unused runnable repo whose homepage, all-products page, contact page, product imagery, nav, cart icon, and footer are deterministic under a simple HTTP server. The task repairs a mobile horizontal-overflow regression in the product-grid purchase-readiness toolbar: the reference reflows the toolbar row so it wraps within the viewport, while preserving the Wardrobe brand, product grid, all-products route, contact route, and local media. Content and DOM are identical across the reference, the original-with-defect baseline, and a shallow non-fix; the mobile no-horizontal-overflow gate is the sole discriminator.
